examples.en: I got athlete's foot, so I'm putting medicine on it.

examples.ko: 무좀은 따뜻하고 습한 곳에서 잘 번져요.
examples.en: Athlete's foot spreads easily in warm, humid places.

examples.ko: 무좀 때문에 발가락 사이가 계속 가려워요.
examples.en: Because of athlete's foot, the area between my toes keeps itching.

examples.ko: 무좀에 걸린 가족과 수건을 따로 써야 해요.
examples.en: You should use separate towels from a family member with athlete's foot.
I'd had athlete's foot for a long time, so I went to the hospital.
After applying the athlete's foot medicine, it got much better.

explain: '무좀에 걸리다', '무좀이 생기다'처럼 말하고, 약은 '무좀약'이라고 해요. 증상은 주로 가려움이라서 '발이 가렵다'와 같이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I bought athlete's foot medicine at the pharmacy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무좀을 치료하는 약을 한 단어로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A single word for medicine that treats athlete's foot.

phrases.en: I caught athlete's foot at the pool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이 옮은 경우에 '걸리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 걸리다 is used when you catch an illness.

phrases.en: I got athlete's foot on my feet in the summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무좀이 새로 나타났을 때 '생기다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 생기다 is used when athlete's foot newly appears.

explain_en: People say '무좀에 걸리다' or '무좀이 생기다', and the medicine is called '무좀약'. Itching is the typical symptom, so it often comes up together with '발이 가렵다'.

examples.en: I shaved my head before going into the army.
After shaving my head, it felt cool.
He decided to shave his head to become a monk.
A cap suits a shaved head well.
I saw my son with a shaved head for the first time.

examples.ko: 야구부 학생들은 시즌 전에 삭발을 해요.
examples.en: The baseball team students shave their heads before the season.

explain: 삭발은 머리를 거의 밀어 버릴 때 쓰고, 보통 머리를 자를 때는 '이발'이나 '커트'를 써요. '삭발을 하다'로 말하고, 군대, 운동부, 스님, 굳은 각오를 보여 줄 때 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: He shaved his head to show his determination.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삭발'에 '하다'가 붙은 동사예요. 머리를 거의 밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of '삭발', used for shaving the head nearly bald.

phrases.en: My shaved head felt strange, so I wore a hat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 머리를 민 상태를 뒤의 명사와 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of a shaved head before a noun.

phrases.en: My friend decided to shave his head to join the sports team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 결심이나 각오와 같이 나오는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression that goes with big decisions or resolve.
phrases.en_equiv: to decide to shave one's head

explain_en: 삭발 is for shaving the head almost bald, while an ordinary haircut is '이발' or '커트'. You say '삭발을 하다'. It often comes up with the army, sports teams, monks, or showing strong resolve.

examples.en: I got a chest X-ray at the hospital.
There was no problem on the X-ray.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 엑스레이 사진을 보여 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor showed me the X-ray image.
At the dentist I had an X-ray taken and then got treatment.

examples.ko: 엑스레이가 나오려면 십 분쯤 기다려야 해요.
examples.en: You have to wait about ten minutes for the X-ray.
At the airport they check bags with an X-ray.

explain: 병원에서는 '엑스레이를 찍다'라고 해요. 사진을 찍는 것처럼 '찍다'를 쓰는 게 특징이에요. 더 정확한 검사인 'CT'나 'MRI'와 같이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: My leg hurts, so I have to get an X-ray taken.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말로, 사진처럼 '찍다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common verb pairing at the hospital; Korean uses 'take (a photo)' for X-rays.

phrases.en: I'm getting an X-ray exam at the hospital tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '검사를 받다'와 함께 쓰면 환자 입장에서 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '검사를 받다' it sounds like the patient's point of view.

phrases.example: 병원에 갈 때 지난번 엑스레이 사진을 가져가세요.
phrases.en: Bring your last X-ray image when you go to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찍고 난 결과물인 사진 자체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the resulting image itself.

explain_en: English loanword, everyday word for the X-ray image taken at a hospital (엑스레이 사진) At the hospital you say 엑스레이를 찍다, using 찍다 (take a photo) with it. It often appears together with the more detailed scans CT and MRI.

t90.ax: There was no problem on the X-ray.

examples.en: I ate spoiled food and got gastroenteritis.

examples.ko: 위장염 때문에 이틀 동안 죽만 먹었어요.
examples.en: Because of gastroenteritis, I ate only porridge for two days.
The doctor said it was acute gastroenteritis.
I stayed home from school until the gastroenteritis cleared up.
The child had a fever and vomited from gastroenteritis.

examples.ko: 위장염은 손을 자주 씻으면 예방할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can prevent gastroenteritis by washing your hands often.

explain: 위와 장에 염증이 생겨 배가 아프고 토하거나 설사하는 병이에요. 보통 '위장염에 걸리다'로 말해요. '위장병'은 넓은 말이고 '위장염'은 염증이 있는 병이에요.

phrases.example: 지난주에 위장염에 걸려서 회사에 못 갔어요.
phrases.en: I caught gastroenteritis last week, so I couldn't go to work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병에 걸렸다고 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for saying someone came down with the illness.

phrases.example: 배가 아프고 토하는 것이 위장염 증상이에요.
phrases.en: A stomachache and vomiting are symptoms of gastroenteritis.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병의 모습을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when describing what the illness looks or feels like.

phrases.en: I got medicine for gastroenteritis from the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이나 약국에서 약 이야기를 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about medicine at a hospital or pharmacy.

explain_en: It is an illness where the stomach and intestines are inflamed, causing stomach pain, vomiting or diarrhea. It is usually said as '위장염에 걸리다'. '위장병' is a broad term, while '위장염' is specifically an inflammation.

examples.en: I got a call from the hospital telling me to come in for a retest.
The result was unclear, so they say a retest is needed.
The retest results come out next week.
I went back to the hospital for a retest.
The retest came back normal, so I was relieved.
Does a retest cost money again?

explain: '재검사를 받다', '재검사를 하다'처럼 써요. 건강검진뿐 아니라 제품 품질 검사나 시험에도 쓰지만, 일상에서는 병원 이야기에서 가장 자주 만나요.

phrases.en: The re-test result was normal, so I felt relieved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검사 뒤에 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the outcome of the re-test.

phrases.example: 병원에서 다음 주에 재검사를 하기로 했어요.
phrases.en: The hospital decided to do a re-test next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: '받다'는 환자 입장이고, '하다'는 하는 쪽이나 일정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '받다' is the patient's side; '하다' fits the doing side or scheduling.

phrases.en: I booked the date for the re-test.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원 예약 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in talk about hospital appointments.

explain_en: A repeat medical or technical check (병원 재검사). It is used as '재검사를 받다' or '재검사를 하다'. It also applies to product quality checks and exams, but in daily life you meet it most often in talk about hospitals.

examples.ko: 할머니의 주치의 선생님은 같은 병원에 오래 계세요.
examples.en: Grandmother's regular doctor has been at the same hospital for a long time.
Before the surgery I consulted in detail with my doctor.
My doctor suggested changing the medicine.
The president has a dedicated personal physician.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 이 병원 의사 선생님이 주치의예요.
examples.en: Since I was little, the doctor at this clinic has been my regular doctor.

examples.ko: 주치의는 환자의 건강을 오랫동안 살펴 주는 사람이에요.
examples.en: A regular doctor looks after the patient's health over a long time.

explain: 한 사람의 병을 계속 맡아서 살펴보는 의사예요. 입원했을 때 맡은 의사는 '담당 의사'라고도 하는데, '주치의'는 더 오랜 관계의 느낌이 있어요. '우리 주치의'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I asked my doctor about the medicine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높여 부를 때 '선생님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 선생님 to address the doctor respectfully.

phrases.en: I changed my doctor when I switched hospitals.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 보던 의사를 다른 사람으로 바꿀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when switching to a different regular doctor.

phrases.en: Talk to your doctor before you start exercising.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 대해 의사와 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when discussing your health with your doctor.

explain_en: A doctor who keeps looking after one person's health. A hospital doctor in charge is also called 담당 의사, but 주치의 suggests a longer relationship. People say it like 우리 주치의.

en: to be tight; to be snug

examples.en: These pants are a bit tight at the waist.

examples.ko: 이번 주 일정이 너무 타이트해서 쉴 틈이 없어요.
examples.en: This week's schedule is so tight that I have no time to rest.
A tight shirt is uncomfortable to move in.

examples.ko: 올해는 예산이 타이트해서 큰 행사는 어려워요.
examples.en: The budget is tight this year, so a big event is difficult.
The jeans got tighter after washing.
The deadline was tight, but the team pulled it off.

explain: 옷은 '꽉 끼다', 일정과 예산은 '빠듯하다'라고 해도 돼요. 타이트하다는 외래어라 직장이나 패션 이야기에서 특히 자주 들려요. 반대는 옷이면 '헐렁하다', 일정이면 '여유 있다'예요.

phrases.en: Tight clothes are uncomfortable if you wear them for long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서는 '타이트한'으로 써요. 몸에 꽉 끼는 옷을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 타이트한 before a noun. It means clothes that fit snugly on the body.

phrases.en: This skirt isn't tight, so it's comfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형이에요. 옷이 꽉 끼지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when clothes are not tight.

phrases.en: My living expenses are tight this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '타이트하다'와 같은 뜻으로, 시간과 돈이 모자랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 타이트하다 for when time or money is just barely enough.

explain_en: Loanword — clothes fit closely, or strict schedules. For clothes you can say 꽉 끼다 and for schedules or budgets 빠듯하다 instead. 타이트하다 is a loanword that you hear especially in work and fashion talk. The opposite is 헐렁하다 for clothes and 여유 있다 for schedules.

t90.ax: The jeans got tighter after washing.

examples.en: The groom was wearing a black tuxedo.
People usually wear a bow tie with a tuxedo.

examples.ko: 턱시도는 파티나 결혼식 같은 큰 행사에 입어요.
examples.en: A tuxedo is worn at big events such as parties or weddings.
A photo of a cat in a tuxedo pattern was popular.
He is a person who looks good in a tuxedo.
It is fine to wear a suit instead of a tuxedo.

explain: '정장'은 면접이나 회사에서 입는 양복이고, 턱시도는 결혼식이나 시상식 같은 격식 있는 저녁 행사에 입는 예복이에요. 검은 털과 하얀 털이 섞인 고양이를 '턱시도 고양이'라고 부르기도 해요.

phrases.en: I will wear a tuxedo at the wedding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷을 입는다고 말할 때 '입다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '입다' to say someone wears the outfit.

phrases.example: 우리 집 턱시도 고양이는 발이 하얘요.
phrases.en: Our tuxedo cat has white paws.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검은 털과 하얀 털이 섞인 고양이를 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Name for a cat with mixed black and white fur.

phrases.en: I rented a tuxedo for the wedding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예복은 사지 않고 빌려 입는 경우가 많아서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used since formal wear is often rented, not bought.

explain_en: 정장 is the suit worn to interviews or the office, while a 턱시도 is formal wear for formal evening events such as weddings or award ceremonies. A cat with mixed black and white fur is also called a '턱시도 고양이'.

examples.en: Busan is at the southeastern end of Korea.

examples.ko: 우리 방은 남동쪽 창문으로 햇빛이 들어와요.
examples.en: In my room, sunlight comes in through the southeast window.
The news says a typhoon is coming up from the southeast.

examples.ko: 우리가 묵을 호텔은 역의 남동쪽에 있어요.
examples.en: The hotel where we will stay is southeast of the station.

examples.ko: 지도를 보면서 남동쪽 방향으로 쭉 가세요.
examples.en: Looking at the map, go straight toward the southeast.

examples.ko: 집이 남동쪽을 향해 있어서 아침이 밝아요.
examples.en: The house faces southeast, so the mornings are bright.

explain: '남동쪽'과 '동남쪽'을 둘 다 써요. 일기예보·지도에서는 '남동풍'처럼 '남동'을 쓰고, '동남아시아'처럼 굳은 이름에는 '동남'이 들어가요. 영어 southeast와 같은 순서가 '남동', 반대 순서가 '동남'이에요. 길을 설명할 때는 '남동쪽 방향'처럼 방향을 붙이기도 해요.

phrases.en: My house is southeast of the station.
phrases.nuance_ko: '남동쪽'과 같은 방향이고 일상 대화에서 둘 다 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same direction as 남동쪽; both are used in daily talk.

phrases.en: Keep going southeast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 알려 줄 때 방향에 '으로'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 으로 to the direction when giving directions.

phrases.en: A southeast wind is blowing today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일기예보에서 '남동'은 바람 이름에 자주 붙어요.
phrases.nuance_en: In weather reports 남동 is often attached to wind.

explain_en: Southeast as a place or side, used alone in daily speech (남동쪽으로 가다); the bare form stays in compounds. Both '남동쪽' and '동남쪽' are used. Forecasts and maps use '남동' (as in '남동풍', southeast wind), while set names like '동남아시아' (Southeast Asia) contain '동남'. '남동' has the same order as English 'southeast' (south first); '동남' is the reverse. When giving directions you can add 방향: '남동쪽 방향'.

t90.ax: Busan is at the southeastern end of Korea.

examples.ko: 대학 때문에 열여덟 살에 서울로 상경했어요.
examples.en: I moved up to Seoul at eighteen for university.
My father went up to Seoul to find a job.

examples.ko: 시골에서 상경한 지 벌써 십 년이에요.
examples.en: It's already been ten years since I came up from the countryside.
I'm going up to Seoul briefly tomorrow for some documents.
Be sure to contact me when you come up to Seoul.
He went up to Seoul carrying his dream.

explain: 지방에서 서울로 올라갈 때만 써요. 말할 때는 '올라가다'가 더 자연스럽고, 반대로 지방으로 갈 때는 '내려가다'라고 해요. '서울로 상경하다'는 뜻이 겹친다고 보는 사람도 있지만 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I'm going up to Seoul tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '상경하다'보다 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural in speech than 상경하다.

phrases.en: I came to Seoul at twenty and have lived here since.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서울에 와서 사는 이야기에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about coming to Seoul and living there.
phrases.en_equiv: to move to Seoul and live

phrases.example: 다음 달에 일 때문에 상경할 거예요.
phrases.en: I'll go to Seoul next month for work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 서울에 갈 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state a plan to go to Seoul.

explain_en: It is only used for going from the provinces to Seoul. In speech '올라가다' sounds more natural, and going the other way is '내려가다'. Some people say '서울로 상경하다' is redundant, but it is common.

examples.en: This is my first Lunar New Year in a foreign land.
The scenery of that distant land was as beautiful as a photo.

examples.ko: 이국적인 음식을 먹으러 새 가게에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to a new restaurant to eat exotic food.

examples.ko: 여행을 가서 이국 사람들과 금방 친해졌어요.
examples.en: On my trip I quickly became friends with people from another country.

examples.ko: 그 카페는 분위기가 이국 느낌이라 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That cafe is popular because it has an exotic feel.
I lived alone in a foreign land for a long time.

explain: '이국'은 글이나 노래에서 주로 보여요. 말할 때는 '외국'이 훨씬 자연스러워요. '이국적이다'는 낯설고 신선한 분위기를 칭찬할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: This street feels really exotic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외국 같고 낯선 분위기가 좋을 때 써요. 말할 때는 '이국'보다 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: For a pleasantly foreign, unfamiliar feel; heard more often than '이국' in speech.

phrases.en: In a foreign land, I missed food from home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먼 외국에서 사는 외로운 느낌이 있고, 글이나 노래에서 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries a lonely feeling of living far abroad; common in writing and songs.

phrases.example: 이국의 음악을 들으니 여행 생각이 났어요.
phrases.en: Hearing foreign music made me think of traveling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이국의 + 명사' 형태로 글에서 분위기를 낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The pattern '이국의 + noun' adds atmosphere in writing.

explain_en: Literary, a strange and unfamiliar foreign land (이국의 풍경) '이국' appears mostly in writing and songs. In speech, '외국' sounds far more natural. '이국적이다' is often used to praise a place or look that feels unfamiliar and fresh.

t90.ax: I went to a new restaurant to eat exotic food.

en: to make a round; to travel around; to make a tour

examples.en: I cycled all the way around Jeju Island.
Traveling around the world is my dream.

examples.ko: 내년에 배낭을 메고 유럽을 일주할 거예요.
examples.en: Next year I'll tour around Europe with a backpack.

examples.ko: 친구와 섬을 일주하고 나서 맛집에 갔어요.
examples.en: After going around the island with a friend, we went to a great restaurant.
Even by bus, one day is enough to go all the way around.

examples.ko: 호수를 일주해 보니 생각보다 길이 험했어요.
examples.en: After going around the lake, I found the path rougher than I expected.

explain: '제주도 일주', '세계 일주'처럼 큰 곳을 한 바퀴 크게 도는 여행에 써요. 동네를 한 바퀴 도는 건 '돌다', '산책하다'를 써요. 보통 '일주를 하다'보다 '일주하다'로 붙여 말해요.

phrases.en: Someday I want to travel all around Europe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 곳을 한 바퀴 돌고 싶은 꿈이나 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for a dream or plan to go all the way around a big place.

phrases.example: 친구와 제주도 일주 여행을 계획하고 있어요.
phrases.en: I'm planning a trip around Jeju Island with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사로 써서 한 바퀴 도는 여행 전체를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a noun, it refers to the whole trip around a place.

phrases.en: It takes two days to go around Jeju Island.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 바퀴 도는 시간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say how long a full lap takes.

explain_en: It is used for a trip that goes once all the way around a large place, as in '제주도 일주' or '세계 일주'. Walking around a neighborhood is '돌다' or '산책하다'. People usually say '일주하다' as one word rather than '일주를 하다'.

examples.en: The car body was badly dented in the accident.

examples.ko: 이 차는 차체가 가벼워서 연비가 좋아요.
examples.en: This car has a light body, so the fuel economy is good.
The shop repainted the car body.
A scratch mark appeared on the car body.
The bus body is long, so turning is difficult.
Electric cars have the battery under the car body.

explain: 자동차에서 엔진, 바퀴, 의자를 뺀 겉 몸체를 말할 때 써요. 정비소나 자동차 설명에서 '차체 수리', '차체 무게'로 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 그냥 '차'라고 하지만 정비나 판매 이야기에서는 '차체'를 구분해서 말해요.

phrases.en: After the accident, I had the car body repaired.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정비소에서 겉 몸체를 고칠 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used at repair shops for fixing the outer body of a car.

phrases.en: This car's body weighs 1.5 tons.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자동차를 설명할 때 무게를 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when describing a car's weight.

phrases.en: The car body damage is severe because of the collision.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고로 겉 몸체가 망가졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the body is damaged in an accident.

explain_en: It means the main body shell of a car, apart from the engine, wheels, and seats. You hear it at repair shops and in car specs, as in 차체 수리 and 차체 무게. In daily talk people just say 차, but 차체 is separated out for repairs and sales.
